summary: The WHSCDA opposes limiting E-Rate eligibility for Head Start and pre-K programs based on the age of children, arguing that screen time is not an appropriate measure of technology infrastructure needs for educational programs. The text argues against limiting or sunsetting E-Rate support for Head Start programs, emphasizing the importance of reliable connectivity for various educational and administrative functions in community-based programs. The text argues against restricting E-Rate support based on age for Pre-K and Head Start programs, emphasizing the disproportionate impact on programs that serve vulnerable children and families. It highlights the potential financial burden on these programs and the need to maintain funding for educational and other program needs. The comment raises concerns about the impact of limiting or sunsetting E-Rate funding on WHSCDA's budget and the availability of resources for other program needs. It highlights the potential consequences of connectivity support removal on the services provided by community-based early childhood programs. The comment also emphasizes the importance of considering the real-world consequences of such changes from the perspective of the organizations delivering services.
